page: Vultr voc-c-2c-4gb-50s-amd is an Optimized Cloud Compute server featuring 2 dedicated vCPUs powered by an AMD EPYC processor running at 2.0 GHz. The hardware configuration includes 1 physical core with 2 threads per core, utilizing the x86_64 architecture. It is equipped with 4.0 GB of system memory, providing 2.0 GB of RAM per core, and includes 50 GB of local NVMe SSD storage. The CPU supports advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512, including AVX512F, AVX512_VNNI, and AVX512_BF16, alongside cryptographic acceleration via AES, VAES, and SHA_NI.

Benchmark data reveals a stark contrast between single-core and multi-core performance. The server achieves top-tier single-core CPU performance in stress-ng benchmarks, placing in the top 10% with a score of 3434.78. However, its multi-core performance drops to the middle 50% average at 6819.14. Single-threaded compression and decompression tasks perform strongly, with gzip compression reaching 32.16 GB/sec and bzip3 decompression reaching 14.65 GB/sec. Conversely, overall PassMark CPU metrics, including extended instructions, encryption, and physics tests, fall into the bottom 25%. Memory bandwidth is average for large blocks but weak for small cached blocks.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, this server offers dedicated AMD EPYC compute resources and fast NVMe storage at a low entry point, making it highly resource-dense for lightweight compute-bound tasks. However, significant performance bottlenecks exist in database operations and web serving; PassMark database operations and Redis SET operations both rank in the bottom 25%, while static web serving throughput is poor, placing in the bottom 10% at 2.49 GB/sec. Consequently, this instance is best suited for single-threaded processing, lightweight background workers, basic CI/CD tasks, or small-scale LLM inference text generation using small models, rather than high-throughput web serving or heavy database workloads.
